newsitem.title: EGYPT: Iran, Qatar are helping Sudan, opposition.
newsitem.headline: Iran, Qatar are helping Sudan, opposition.

text.p: Iran and Qatar are supplying the Islamist Sudanese government with military equipment, expertise and money in its fight against rebel forces, a Sudanese opposition group said on Sunday.

"Iran has provided weapons, military equipment, pilots and technicians to support the Sudanese regime in confronting the Sudanese opposition forces," the National Democratic Alliance said in a statement in Cairo.
"Qatar has also given Sudan financial and military support," it added. "We see it cooperate with Iran in sending military equipment to Sudan."
The NDA mentioned details of the alleged Iranian interference, warning Tehran from its consequences.

"Within the past few days, more than 25 Iranian military technicians and experts arrived into the Wadi Sidna military base in Omdurman (Sudan)," said the statement, signed by the NDA's spokesman Mubarak el-Mahdi.
"This flagrant interference by Iran in Sudan's internal affairs with money, armour and men, is dangerous and unacceptable," it added.

"The Iranian support to the Islamic Front (in Sudan) is not an internal affair, as its consequences would have an important dimension on the security and stability in the African Horn and the Red Sea area, particularly in Egypt, Saudi Arabia and the Gulf states."
The group called on Qatar to stop what it called weapon supplies to Khartoum and cooperation with Iran and Islamic militant groups.
Sudanese opposition forces, bent on toppling the Islamist government of Khartoum, have launched just over a month ago an offensive across Sudan's eastern and southern borders.

Sudan has accused Ethiopia, Eritrea and Uganda of direct military involvement in the rebel offensive. Both countries deny any involvement in the conflict and the rebels say that they alone are waging the offensive.

A senior Iranian official is currently in Khartoum in a mediation bid between Sudan and Uganda. Sudanese President Omar Hassan al-Bashir received Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Hossein Sheikholeslam on Saturday, the Sudanese television said.
It quoted Bashir as saying during the meeting that his country was "committed to the Iranian initiative seeking to resolve the differences" between Sudan and Uganda through peaceful means.

Sheikholeslam, whose country has strong relations with Sudan, told the television that he hoped to hold meetings next month with Ugandan officials in Kampala in a bid to settle differences between Sudan and Uganda.
He handed Bashir a letter from Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani on bilateral relations and the Iranian initiative, the television said.
Sheikholeslam also met Sudanese Foreign Minister Ali Osman Mohammad Taha, it added.
